utterances.text: Let's go to the next exhibit, the map, 439. And there are three locations depicted in orange, one Donji Vecerska, but the other two, what are those other two locations?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: If you go southwest, you come to the ring, the orange ring, that's Sesilja, that's a village that I visited early on that had an ethnic mix that was in the possession of the HVO but fell about this time to the BiH, and that's what Kraljevic had told me that he had been sent to re-establish or to repossess on behalf of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how about feature 1105?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Feature 1105 was a key strategic point as far as both the HVO and the BiH were concerned because it overlooked the area, Muslim area, of Kruscica and was -- the troops in charge of that particular point were allowed to see vantage and viewpoint over the Lasva Valley in order to coordinate fire, so it was important to both of them. It was initially the territory of the HVO but fell again at about the same time to the BiH who were subsequently able to organise movements through the -- from the south into Kruscica and supplement their own position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the taking position of feature 1105 important to the military strategy of the HVO in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I can, Mr. President, move to the next video, which is Exhibit 440. Again, this is a BBC video commentary by Martin Bell, you will see the date in the video itself I believe is the 14th October, 1993, and if we could dim the lights and move to that next video? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can wind that back, please? Stop there. Back up. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stop.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's the man you know as Darko Kraljevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Kraljevic is on the right and the chap to his left was his deputy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the feature that they were exploding was feature 1105; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continue on with the tape. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person speaking on behalf of this action was Blaskic's liaison officer, is it not?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, it's Darko Gelic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, based on your activity as a liaison officer in Central Bosnia, in conjunction with the evidence that you've discussed here today, did you see or did you conclude that what Blaskic wrote in this order, Exhibit 422, was, in fact, correct, that the Vitezovi was an independent unit under his command?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I did, sir, yeah. The fact that Gelic was making the statements he was making on behalf of the HVO and Kraljevic clearly had been instructed to carry out that action on behalf of HVO and Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you a Defence Exhibit, Defence 137, if I may, which is a portion of a milinfosum introduced by counsel of the 8th of August, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm having a bit of a tough time with the monitor here, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It's not just you. We're also having difficulty. All right. Is that okay now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I figured out the combination. My colleague, Mr. Harmon, said press the top button first so ... the top button and the second button, and it seems to work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SHAHABUDDEEN
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, you're a real star because the only thing I see on the screen is you. I don't see any document here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: How depressing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No. For the time being -- oh, I see -- is you. Okay. Now I have the transcript. I don't have the video. There you go. Thank you, Judge Shahabuddeen. Very well. We can go forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you see the document D137?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is a conversation by a Borislav Jozic related to you; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It was indeed, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was Borislav Jozic?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: He was one of the officers of Mario Cerkez who was responsible for supervising and organising the exchange of bodies with his opposite number in the BiH. I liaised between the two. Wasn't a key military figure and was pretty poorly informed in that respect, but he was a local -- I think he was an ex-policeman or something like that who was quite a nice chap but had the onerous task of doing the body exchanges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Captain, in the second-to-last line of this Jozic note, it tells you that he, Jozic, further claimed that they, the Vitezovi, were not effectively under Blaskic's control. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yes, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he tell you that?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That was his impression, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree with that impression?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: No, I don't, sir. I think that was effectively supposition on his part. He was not really, as I mentioned earlier, conversant with the structures that were operating in the Hotel Vitez and didn't really have a lot to do with military matters and the HVO, was simply an HVO representative for organising the body exchanges.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Gelic or Blaskic or anybody in the Hotel Vitez indicate to you at any time that the Vitezovi was not under the command of the Defendant Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Not at any time, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, sir, did you see any linkage between the local HVO brigades, under Mario Cerkez, and the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Mario Cerkez was actually a close friend and comrade of Darko Kraljevic, they spoke very fondly and often about each other, and on one particular occasion, I met them together up at the Donji Vecerska headquarters because obviously it was Mario Cerkez's brigade area that Kraljevic was trying to regain ground for.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During any of your negotiations or any conversations with Cerkez concerning the release of any hostages, did Cerkez try to factor in any release of HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yes, he did so, on one particular occasion, some members of the Croat population in Vitez came to me and explained that their three sons had been taken hostage and captured by the Armija in Kruscica. I visited Kruscica, spoke to their local Armija commander in Kruscica, and he allowed me to see the three young lads who were about 13, 14, and 15, and they were being housed quite comfortably in the local civilian police quarters in Kruscica area. I arranged with the local -- I tried to arrange with the local commander for the release of the three boys but was ineffective initially. Shortly afterwards, Mario Cerkez stopped an ICRC vehicle who were removing people from Stari Vitez on medical grounds, they were evacuating two casualties from Stari Vitez. Mario Cerkez's troops stopped the ICRC vehicle and removed the two casualties and held them captive as prisoners and then offered them in exchange for the three children who were being held in Kruscica. I then re-set up an exchange of -- exchange the three boys for the two casualties that Mario Cerkez was now holding in the cellar of the cinema. On that particular day, I went to collect three boys and left a representative of mine with Mario Cerkez's headquarters and the two casualties. I retrieved the three boys in an armoured vehicle and was sat in no man's land between the HVO and BiH frontlines waiting for confirmation from my sergeant that the boy -- the two casualties had been released to him, and it was at this time that Mario Cerkez said that the exchange was not going to go ahead until, in addition to the three boys, three members of the Vitezovi that were allegedly in the possession of the BiH were also added to the exchange, i.e., so the two casualties taken from the ICRC would be released when we -- the three boys and the three members of the Vitezovi who were allegedly held by the BiH were released into my possession to be brought back to Mario Cerkez and the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mario Cerkez was the HVO brigade commander in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he wanted to get three Vitezovi soldiers back as part of this exchange?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: He did indeed, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there some connection there between the Vitezovi and the Viteska brigade?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: There was a very strong connection as far as I was concerned. Not only were they the Vitezovi working on behalf of the HVO to support and help them attain their military goals in regaining the ground lost, but there was a close liaison and friendship between Mario Cerkez and Darko Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can move ahead, and we'd like to go back to some of these photos and before we talk about Stari Vitez very briefly let me just chat for one moment about the first two photographs, these two, which will be -- which are these? 433/13 and 433/14 again, Captain, these are a series of photographs which you took, many of which are now in evidence, where General Prelak with Blaskic came to Novi Bila hospital, is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: General Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Petkovic, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Is the bald chap in the middle, to the right of him is Colonel Blaskic, and to the right of him, in the background, is one of the military police personal bodyguards of Colonel Blaskic and to the right but to the foreground is the liaison officer from Kiseljak of the HVO. The people to the left of Colonel Petkovic, General Petkovic, are in the background are two representatives from Kiseljak and the U.N. overseeing the triage and the two people in white coats are the doctors from the Novi Bila hospital.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next photograph is, in fact, you and Petkovic and the liaison officer, Vinko Lucic, from Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Usher. Let us turn, if you will, to Stari Vitez very briefly. Captain, what was your assessment of the HVO strategy in Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Stari Vitez seemed a very convenient bargaining chip, really, for the HVO, it was a very small pocket of Muslims, there was no real Armija soldiers in there, they were all local militia, there was a large number of women and children, families who were originally living in the Stari Vitez area, and really, I saw that as a bargaining chip/lever used by the HVO on numerous occasions to release pressure brought to bear by them by the BiH from the Zenica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what sense? Explain that.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: If there were any military action conducted against the Lasva Valley area or any shelling or any military activity, then they had on their doorstep a small Muslim enclave in the form of Stari Vitez which they could apply pressure to. The commander Sefkija, in the centre of Stari Vitez, had direct communications to the troops and people in the Muslim community in Zenica, and so, very quickly, he could communicate to them that a lot of pressure was being brought to bear on Stari Vitez. So, for example, if there were any military action by the BiH onto the Lasva pocket, then it was very easy for the HVO to then -- to shell or to apply military pressure to Stari Vitez. Stari Vitez would then communicate to Zenica to say, "Stop whatever it is you're doing because we're taking casualties at this particular end." And that seemed an effective tool as far as we were concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What type of pressure did the HVO put on Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: They employed what were affectionately known as "babies," there was regular small-arm sniping on a daily basis, but periodically they would up the level of activity and aggression towards Stari Vitez by launching mortars and these improvised mortar bombs called "babies" or fire extinguisher bombs into the Stari Vitez enclave, obviously causing a considerable amount of damage and numerous casualties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Explain to us something about these "babies." Are they indiscriminate and why are they indiscriminate?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: A "baby" is a fire extinguisher packed full of home-made explosive or explosive that is obviously produced in the ammunition factory. It doesn't really have a cushion cap, it just has a fuse, and there is an improvised tube welded together in which its led and then a firing charge is put underneath it which launches the fire extinguisher through the air, throwing it maybe 400 or 500 metres up in the air and forward a couple of hundred metres. That then lands, the fuse burns down, and the fire extinguisher full of home-made explosive explodes to great effect with a rather large bang. It's a very poorly aimed weapon with a very limited range and you can't guarantee it going off when it lands and neither can you guarantee the direction in which it's going to -- or the area in which it's going to fall, so they're just lobbed in the general direction of where you want to create the most damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it can hit either civilians or a military target?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me show you Exhibit 82/7, and I believe this is another photograph taken by you. I may be mistaken --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 82/5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Five. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that a photograph of one of the "babies," sir?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It is indeed, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take that photograph?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I did indeed. That was taken in Stari Vitez. It's actually got the date on it that it landed within the confines of the Stari Vitez enclave.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that would be what date?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It's the 9th of September -- 9th of July, '93.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did there come a time when you were blocked from going into Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Quite early on in the tour. The west -- the road coming from the West I. from BRITBAT into Stari Vitez was completely blocked off by a large lorry allegedly stuffed full of local home-made explosive, it actually had the words "Dynamite" painted on the side, but in addition to that, there was rocks and earth piled up and several anti-personnel and anti-armour mines placed around the vehicle itself, so it was a complete obstacle as far as we were concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn to this photograph which is part of the 433 series. That's 433 -- I'm sorry, Mr. Usher, what's the number on the back of that? THE USHER: The number is 15.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 433/15. Is that a photograph that you took, Captain?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It is indeed, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to the explosive device that you were just discussing in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yeah. This is the road coming from -- so BRITBAT is approximately about a mile off the bottom of the picture, it approached Stari Vitez which is literally on the other side of this vehicle here that's got "TNT" written on it. There are several mines placed underneath the vehicle and around the vehicle and a large pile of earth and rocks, and allegedly there was TNT stuffed in the vehicle as well as the mines placed in the water around the front of the obstacle itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, that is on the backside of Stari Vitez going towards BRITBAT.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the front side, moving toward Vitez, did that receive the brunt of the attack on the "babies"?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It did indeed so, yeah. It was the eastern side, where the majority of the "babies" were launched, were either Vitez town centre side of Stari Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we turn to the next photograph? This is 433/16. Again, a photograph taken by you?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It is indeed, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Housing in the back; is that an example of the blast damage from "babies"?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It is, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just for -- to put this in perspective, let's move to the next photograph, which is 433/17. Is that the trenching area on the Muslim side of Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yeah, it is, sir. The wall, the perimeter wall there, you can see is about 200 or 300 metres. On the other side of that is Vitez town centre. In fact, you can actually make out, on the right-hand side, the blocks of flats in the centre of Vitez there. That's at the top end of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is this, as the crow flies, if you will, from the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Five hundred, 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would someone sitting in the Hotel Vitez be aware of the indiscriminate shelling with "babies" being done on Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Absolutely so, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, there was a time -- thank you, sir. There was a time when aid was cut off, was it not?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: There was indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why was that?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: The HVO alleged that I had been supplying weapons, munitions, to the BiH and also moving troops in and out of the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that true?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there ever an occasion that ammunition was smuggled in without your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: There was one occasion where an attempt was made to use me to smuggle a small amount of ammunition in, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was that about?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I had been asked to take some medical supplies into Stari Vitez and picked up several small boxes of medical supplies from the UNHCR building in Zenica, which was a Muslim enclave, took them into Stari Vitez, handed them over to Commander Sefkija. He immediately handed them over to one of his subordinates who took them away to another room. I sat and drank coffee and exchanged pleasantries of the day, assessing the situation with Commander Sefkija, and then shortly after decided -- made an excuse to leave and took a walk around the houses and buildings adjacent to Commander Sefkija's headquarters. I walked into a room and found them unpacking the boxes that were allegedly full of bandages, and inside each of the bandages was a box of 20 rounds of ammunition. So there was maybe 600 or 1.000 rounds in total that if each box had contained, you know, 400 or 500 rounds, so they had managed to wrap a carton of 20 rounds in a bandage, basically, and then stick a box full of bandages in the back of my vehicle. When I found that out, I got very annoyed with Commander Sefkija, left after expressing my disappointment that, as far as I was concerned, he must have been aware that this was going to happen or it had been happening and that he had betrayed my trust, and I stopped all subsequent deliveries of medical supplies into Stari Vitez and those were only conducted by the ICRC on an official basis from that point onwards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this period of time, during your tour, did you have conversations with Darko Gelic as to what the overall strategy was of the HVO if the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina attempted to take over the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: They said it wasn't going to happen, that it would be met with determined resistance, and if all else failed, they would end up blowing up the ammunition factory and everything in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Blaskic make such allegations as well?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, he did so, yes. He actually informed Colonel Alastair of that at a meeting that I had arranged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What would have been the net result to the Lasva Valley of such an explosion?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: There would have been a large number of casualties, both civilian and military, in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Gelic ever comment to you about what they would do to Zenica if such an invasion by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina took place?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: He did indeed. On one of the regular replies, as I think I mentioned earlier, to any determined BiH military offensive onto the Lasva Valley was for them to employ one of their large howitzers, effectively known as "Nora," they would lob 155-millimetre shells into the centre of Zenica, and on several occasions, civilians were killed due to the blast from these shells.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you conclude was the reason for such a strategy?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It was a tit-for-tat exchange saying quite clearly to the BiH, "Don't try anything because we're quite prepared to do whatever it takes to put you off."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And "put you off," what do you mean "put you off"?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: "To deter you launching any offensive onto the Lasva Valley area."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're going to change subjects again, Captain, and move to the 5th of July, 1993, and the killing of Dobrila Kolaba and your participation in that investigation. Can you talk to the Judges briefly about that, your participation in the investigation, and what the HVO conclusion was?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Do you want me to recount the incident itself?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, briefly.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I can't quite remember the dates. On one particular evening, a small arms exchange had broken out around the BRITBAT location. Several of the officers were accommodated in buildings outside the actual fence of the BRITBAT location, and living in amongst us in those houses were some of the interpreters who were local to the area, one of which was the Colonel's personal interpreter, a young lady named Dobrila who was actually a Serb. On one side of the BRITBAT location, there were HVO Croats' trenches and frontlines, and on the other were the BiH, and so there were regular small arms exchange in and around the camp area. On this particular occasion, after two or three hours, there was an increase in the level of small arms fire, and the Captains' House, as it was known, where two of the interpreters resided downstairs and myself and two of the captains lived on the upstairs floor, was raked with small arms fire. Dobrila was shot through the head during that exchange. I was made responsible by the Colonel for investigating the incident with a view to finding out who had been responsible and punishing those responsible, bearing in mind it was a U.N. representative, an interpreter, who had been injured. I went to the Hotel Vitez, and Colonel Blaskic expressed his sympathies about what had happened and said that he would provide an investigative team to assist in finding out who was responsible for Dobrila's death. The investigation lasted two to three days, which I oversaw, I escorted the HVO representatives around the firing point and the impact point where Dobrila had been murdered, and after three days, they reached a conclusion. The conclusion they offered was that a BiH soldier must have crossed over the road into Croat lines, assumed one of the sniper positions in the houses opposite the officers' mess, fired the rounds, and then returned over the road back into the Armija lines.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you think about that?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I think it was rubbish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You didn't believe it?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was any HVO soldier ever punished for this?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's move to the next instance a little more than a month later, the 14th of August, 1993, the killing of a UNHCR driver by the name of Boris in Stari Vitez. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I am indeed, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us about it.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: The UNHCR at this particular point had relatively free and safe passage in the area but would nevertheless come into BRITBAT, register with myself as the area liaison officer, and tell me what they were up to and leave instructions with the headquarters. On this particular occasion, they came in. I wasn't there. They left, headed back down the road to Vitez because -- went and drove through the town centre of Vitez, entered Stari Vitez through the chicane, and on entering Stari Vitez, were sniped at with a large .5 inch calibre weapon which resulted in the death of Boris.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to -- by the way, a .5 inch round is also known as a 12.7 --

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: 12.7 millimetre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- millimetre round. It's a pretty significantly sized round, is it not?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: A very significantly sized round, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to put this in perspective, if we could then move to this particular map. Before we move to this map, after the killing of Boris, did you go back and analyse the ground to check the firing point and to see, based on the point of impact, where the firing point was?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I did indeed, sir, conduct a very thorough investigation over the next two days and then I had to present myself to several senior U.N. representatives who flew up from Zagreb who wanted me to present all the information and evidence to them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention to this map --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 441.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using the pointer with Exhibit 441, could you help us, first, to show the path that Boris took when he was driving up to the BRITBAT camp and the path he took returning to go back into Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Can we open the picture out a little bit more?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we just pan it back just a little bit? Maybe just move it down just a little bit, Mr. Usher?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: This is the main road coming from Zenica and the BRITBAT location is down this end here, so Dorothy, who was the UNHCR field officer, and Boris would have driven along this road, past -- along the road to BRITBAT, left a message that they were going to Stari Vitez; then they would have gone back along this road, because there was no access into Stari Vitez because of the blockade that we saw earlier down here, they would have gone back down past this point, turned right, entering the town of Vitez, passing through the chicane about here, and entering the area of Stari Vitez, and at this point here, the vehicle would have been slowing down to turn and meet with Commander Sefkija whose headquarters are about here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the left-hand side of this photograph, there's a somewhat broken line in orange. What does that depict, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: There was somewhere along this particular stretch, and my memory escapes me which side of this garage thing it was, what we call a sanger, which is a trench with overhead cover, a well-established firing trench.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Controlled by what unit?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: By the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: And I examined closely the impact point and the vehicle. The round went through the right-hand side of the vehicle, i.e. it was moving in this direction, so it could only have come from this particular side of the road, and this was an account given to me by the woman who survived the incident, who was the UNHCR field officer. And this area here, this junction (indicated) --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're pointing to the arrow, where the arrow is.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Where the arrow is -- whilst there are houses there, there are several large gaps between the houses that allow a clear field of view across to this sanger, and, in fact, all these houses and trees here are riddled with small arms marks because this was a regular site where the occupants of Stari Vitez were sniped at by the HVO forces from this established trench position on this side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there any question in your mind that there was no mistake, that this was a UNHCR vehicle?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: The vehicle is white, it would have transited this point on three occasions immediately prior to going -- on two occasions immediately prior to going into here, and at several points along its journey, it's quite easy to see the vehicle's progress as it progresses along this road. This is open field area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is it from the firing point into Stari Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: About 700 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn your attention to the next photograph in the 433 series. Mr. Usher ... THE USHER: Number 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 433/18. What is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's the round that was embedded in the front windscreen. It's actually finished its journey there. It entered through the right-hand side of the vehicle, it was deflected by the kevlar plating, went through the back of Boris, out through his heart, and then wedged itself, embedded itself in the front windscreen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This round is not coming in, it's actually after going through his body, lodging itself with the blunt end in the windscreen?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: What it hit the kevlar, it started spinning, which is what ripped the front of his chest out, and therefore it stuck, in an obtuse angle, into the windscreen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequent to this, did you have conversations with anyone in the HVO about this event?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I attempted to investigate it in the same way that I had with Dobrila, got the military police involved from BRITBAT, and they were offering to assign a team from Hotel Vitez, from the HVO as well. There was instant denial of it being any HVO soldier --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who instantly denied that?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Darko Gelic. And when I showed him the round, he said, "Well, we don't have any weapon of that calibre, we don't possess anything of that particular type, but I do know that they produced those calibre of weapons in the Zenica steel factory." The investigation quickly ground to a halt because Commander Sefkija, the BiH commander in Stari Vitez, would not let any member of the HVO into the area to investigate the impact point, i.e. where Boris had actually been shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to a couple of exhibits in the 82 -- Exhibit 82, Mr. Dubuisson?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 82/9 and 82/10.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could also use this photograph as well, which is part of the 433 series, which is 433 -- which one, Mr. Usher? THE USHER: Nineteen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Gelic told you that they didn't have any such weapon to fire a 12.7 millimetre round or a .5 inch round; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that such rounds were made in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's right, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thereafter, did you find such a weapon?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I did indeed, sir, yeah. There was one in possession of Darko Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Indeed, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you take photographs of have weapon?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the first photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will you please slow down a little bit because of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 82/9. Using the pointer, point to the weapon that would shoot a 12.7 millimetre round.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: (Indicated)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the weapon that the individual has in his left hand? I think there is yet another angle of it in 82/10, and lastly, a single photograph of it on 433/19. Now, how rare is that weapon, Captain?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: They're an American specialist sniper rifle. They're very rare, used by the IRA, but they're pretty manufactured-to-order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see another one in Bosnia when you were there, much less in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Nope.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you conclude when you saw this weapon in the possession of the Vitezovi?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: They were a specialist branch of the HVO forces. They were equipped with everything that they needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you conclude about this weapon in relation to the killing of Boris?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That that was the only weapon I saw during my time in Bosnia that was capable of taking one single shot from 700 metres and doing that sort of damage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you report back to your headquarters that you had, in fact, found the weapon that killed Boris?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: As far as I was concerned, yes, I reported back that that was the weapon, the only weapon that could have been responsible for it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me change subjects, and thank you again. We will move back to the balance of the photographs in one moment. Before we move into the attack on Grbavica, I'd like to talk to you just briefly about the use of the media by the HVO. Did there come a time in August of 1993 where Radio Vitez threatened white vehicles or U.N. vehicles in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: There was a time, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time, were you also personally threatened over the radio or Radio Vitez in the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: There were incidents where I was made particularly unwelcome by members of the HVO at frontline locations as I tried to transit from one area to another, and when asked why, they told me that I was no longer a friend of Croatian people in the Lasva Valley and that they had been instructed that they were not to cooperate with me in any way whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed by Darko Gelic that such a threat had been placed over Radio Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I was indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any instances to conclude that any member of the HVO military staff had some control over what was broadcast on Radio Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I had the pleasure of visiting Mario Cerkez on one day, and he was boasting about some new song, a propaganda song, that had been written locally in an attempt to raise morale of the HVO and the Croatian people, and he had a radio on his desk, and he said to me, you know, "Listen to this. You can hear how good it is." And he promptly banged on the wall, and within minutes, this song appeared on the radio playing on his desk, and understandably, I was quite amazed by this, and he disclosed to me that next door to his office they had a radio station broadcasting news and whatever they thought was necessary to the local people in the cinema.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn our attention to another subject at this point, Captain, and that is the attack on Grbavica on the 7th and 8th of September of 1993. Now, prior to this attack, had both Blaskic and Cerkez noted to you that they were going to have to do something about the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina positions in Stari Bila -- or in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yeah. The Armija had the high-point positions in Grbavica overlooking BRITBAT and the Croat positions on the other side of the road. There were regular small arms exchanges, and therefore, regular casualties, usually on the part of the Croatian populace and military forces, around the BRITBAT location. There were repeated threats by Commander Blaskic that he was going to have to deal with this problem and likewise from Commander Cerkez because they were taking far too many casualties. This threat wasn't actually carried out for some considerable period of time because we regularly reminded Colonel Blaskic that we had -- the colonel had set up an agreement wherein there would be no military action within 500 metres of the BRITBAT location, and that agreement lasted until about the 7th, 8th of September when the HVO launched a full military assault onto the Grbavica position.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, militarily speaking, the attack to remove Bosnian army forces from that ridge was a legitimate military objective; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Absolutely. And very well-executed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Explain the execution to the Judges, if you can?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: From a tactical point of view, it was well-thought and planned out, and troops, they -- what's the word I'm looking for? -- they pummelled and suppressed the position for about 24 hours with small arms, anti-aircraft weapons, mortars, in an attempt to soften up the BiH troops in the Grbavica area, and then that following morning, at dawn, they then launched a carefully planned military assault after taking out the high-point feature.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Let's turn to one of our last exhibits, and that will be this exhibit, Mr. Dubuisson.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 442, 442A for the caption.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using this photograph by the numbers, Captain, can you just tell the Judges exactly how this assault took place following sequentially on the numbers?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Point 1 is a high feature and along which were located several large weapon systems like machine guns, anti-aircraft weapons, and they were involved for the first 24 hours in firing into and suppressing the BiH positions, particularly at this point here, Point 3, which was the high point which overlooked all the HVO positions all along here on this side of the road. This is the BRITBAT location here (indicated), and so on -- this is the main road feature. It runs up here. And on this side effectively is the BiH, and on this side is the HVO. After the first 24 hours, during that 24 hours, there was a lot of fire laid down onto these positions where the Muslim -- there were lots of Muslim people and there were also soldiers of the Armija. The following morning, what then happened was an infantry assault from this point here (indicated), they used the low ground here to move soldiers up the banking, and from this point, they then launched a systematic clearance through these houses, and that's indicated by the large arrow there, clearing through all the houses in this way. There were also troops that came from this area. So 2 is the movement, the infantry movement of troops in, and 3 is then the clearance, systematic clearance, of enemy soldiers and Muslims from that -- from the Grbavica community there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about 4, over to the left?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Just a second. Excuse me. What do you mean by "clearing the houses"?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It's a term we use, i.e. checking each individual house, it's got no soldiers in it, no people in it, so making sure there is nobody in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Making sure there is nobody in it?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Or no weapons in it?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Nobody alive left in them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And if there was somebody alive?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: If there were soldiers, then they would be dealt with accordingly. However, if they surrendered, you would take them as prisoners --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And civilians?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's entirely up to the troops doing the assault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: And here I don't think we found any civilian casualties. We did find two or three bodies, one of which had been beheaded in there, but they did have the items of uniform on them, so we assumed that they were soldiers of the Armija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The point designated number 4?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Four represents the arrow and that was the route taken, the general exodus of the Muslim community during the night of the 7th, still in dark in the morning of the 8th before the infantry attack actually took place. Five was the infantry attack that actually took place in the morning, and during that time, we're assuming that all the civilians had actually left, and there were only a few Armija soldiers still left defending the position. The area had taken a considerable beating with various weapon systems throughout the previous 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Captain, after -- just taking up from Judge Riad's question -- after the village itself was cleared of people, what did the HVO soldiers then do in the village?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: After they had actually been through and cleared it, there was a systematic burning of all the buildings that we saw in there. I actually was sent by Colonel Alastair to go into Vitez and to address Colonel Blaskic and say, "Look, this must stop. It's getting out of hand." I was told that Colonel Blaskic was not available by Darko Gelic who ignored -- who said to me, as far as he was concerned, there was no military action taking place anywhere in the Lasva Valley. And then as I journeyed back up the road from Vitez, I observed numerous soldiers and literally all -- there was some looting going on by the HVO soldiers and all the buildings had been set on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you sent there by Colonel Duncan or the 2-IC?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It wasn't Colonel Duncan, it was Richard Watson, the 2-IC who was present at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Captain, can you tell the difference between damage from artillery fire and damage to houses that are purposely set on fire?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Absolutely, yeah. If it has just been burnt, there is obviously no shrapnel damage, no obvious damage from small arms, and very limited blast damage. A fire is a fire, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we can go to the next video, Mr. President, and I believe the next video is numbered ...

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: 443. Again, this is another BBC video, Mr. President and Your Honours, from the 8th of September, 1993. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If you can roll it back? Stop right there. A little bit further. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stop there. Just back up a little bit. That's good.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Captain, as a military officer, was it necessary for the HVO to burn those houses systematically?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Absolutely not. There were several examples you can see in this film where the buildings have deliberately been set on fire in their foundations to make sure that there was nothing left for anybody to come back to and that they were uninhabitable.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Before we go to those particular houses, I would like to put that frame back on the screen. Can we put that frame back on the screen? I'm not sure it's coming on your screen, Mr. President. It's coming on one screen but not the other screen. Counsel, is it on your screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I've got the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It just came, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Early on in your testimony, you said you observed members of the Jokeri -- can you leave that on the screen, please? -- members of the Jokeri that were involved in the attack on Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I did indeed so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see anybody in that photograph that fits that description from that day?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: The gentleman to the rear dressed in black is typically wearing the type of uniform that I witnessed that day when I met the Jokeri, and I did see that day several insignia and faces that looked familiar to me as if they actually belonged to that organisation. For the most part, these are soldiers I recognise as being part of the TURTKO before the second which is the one we saw detailed on Colonel Blaskic's orders earlier as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we can move ahead on that tape --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Can we make a still, Mr. President, for ease of future reference?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Sure. If we could do that, that would fine, make it the next Prosecutor's Exhibit. (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stop right there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Captain, is that burning from artillery fire or intentional burning, in your opinion?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: The building to the fore looks like it has small arms marks on the outside, but that looks like it's been burnt, the one in the background looks like it's just been set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Could we have another still, Mr. President, to speed my examination so we won't have to take extra time to find these locations?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No problem. We'll make that another Prosecutor's Exhibit. We'll move ahead to another series --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You'll have all the time you need, Mr. Hayman. If you think it's taking a long time, that's how it is. Go ahead, Mr. Kehoe. Mr. Hayman, you will have the time that you need.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Continue just a little bit more on the tape? (Videotape played)

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Stop right there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about that burning?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's the woodpile underneath the house that's been deliberately set on fire to make sure it's levelled to the ground or uninhabitable, at least, by anybody who wants to live in it. So that's not been set on fire by artillery or small arms fire or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: We can make a frame of that as well, whatever the next exhibit happens to be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Subsequent to the attack on Grbavica, did you have a conversation with Mario Cerkez about this particular event?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yes. I was attempting to find out who had been responsible for it, it was a very well-executed and well-planned attack, so I went to see Mario, flattered him about it, said as such, and he admitted to me that he hadn't been responsible for it but it had been planned by the staff officers in the Hotel Vitez and intimated that it had been by, in fact, a chap I know as Filipovic who was a former JNA officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we turn to -- this is a part of Exhibit 80, this particular photograph. It's part of the 80 series, I'm not sure which one in 80 it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe, we've got to think about when we're going to stop. How much more do you have to -- how much more time do you need? Do you think you're going to be finished by 6.00?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I think so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Then continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's the photograph, yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is 80/6.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The photograph that has been received in evidence, 80/6, is the individual that Cerkez -- or that you came to understand was responsible for the success at Grbavica, is he depicted in that photograph?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: He is indeed. He's the gentleman with the white hair, sat on Colonel Blaskic's right or on the left as we look at it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to him with the pointer, please?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: (Indicated)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's just to Blaskic's right and our -- is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: (Indicated)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The individual in the gray hair to his right. When you were up there observing what was going on and the houses were being systematically burnt, did you notice any looting going on as well?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yeah, there was -- I saw numerous instances of soldiers removing items from the houses, I think I actually photographed one of them removing a tape recorder, and there was a lot of looting that took place immediately afterwards by the local population, in fact, who started turning up in large numbers with flatbed trucks, et cetera, to reclaim whatever they could quickly before the place was burnt to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If we could quickly go through the last series of photographs, Mr. Usher, in the 433 series, and what's the first number? THE USHER: First number is number 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Starting with 433/20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Captain, that's a photograph that you took, is it not?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It is, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that of Grbavica prior to the events of the 7th and 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It is indeed, sir, yeah, with the mosque in the bottom there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to 433/21, the next photograph. What is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's a photograph I took as I left Vitez on the way back to BRITBAT, approaching Grbavica. You can make out the mosque which is on the Vitez side as I'm approaching it, and basically all the buildings are on fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are the buildings in and about the mosque on fire as well?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: They are indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to the next one, 433/22.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I think that's the photograph I took originally as I left Vitez. When I turned around, as I was approaching the road, I was quite astounded by the sight of it as I was returning, so that's the first photograph I took, just showing the extent of what was actually burning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photograph, 433/23. Is that just house damage and ...

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yes, those are the two houses really where the Armija set themselves which are the two houses which overlook BRITBAT and the HVO position, so it was those two houses which all the sniping came from effectively.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the next photograph, 433/24?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's a picture I took of some of the soldiers who had been looting in the area. One of them's got a cassette, the other one's carrying what, in fact, was a large butcher's axe, chopping axe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The other has a radio in his hand?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: He has indeed, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to that and point to the axe? The one on the left has the radio --

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's a large chopping axe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: What was it used for?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour, I'm afraid. I can't honestly say other than one of the bodies that was found in there had been decapitated, but I wouldn't make the assumption that that person and weapon was responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: But this is a soldier, the one holding it?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the next photograph, 433/25.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's a similar photograph, just panning back so you can see at close quarters the number of buildings that are being burnt out and the soldiers in the vicinity immediately after the attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 433/26? Just houses burning in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That is, in fact, the house of -- that we saw earlier that my Land Rover was parked outside of that belonged to a woman and her daughter that I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean the same prior to the actual attack?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's right, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Same houses. It's another house in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's actually a picture capturing the HVO using "babies" in their infantry assault the morning of the 8th of September.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you point to that "baby" in there?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yeah. That black mark is actually a fire extinguisher tumbling through there, and you can't make it out very clearly on the screen, but on here there is a white flash -- this photograph actually was in colour, and that was an orange flash. That was the detonation point which launched the "baby" through the air.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next series of photographs, 29, 30, and 31, if you can just look at those? Those are just a series, I believe, of houses burning in Grbavica. If you can just have the witness look at those, that would be fine. That one, the next one, 30, and 31, all houses burning, Captain, on the --

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photograph as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Which village is that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: It's all Grbavica, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Captain?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It's the same village, Your Honour. They're all just shots taken surveying the damage after the attack and the extent to which the burning took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next photograph? What number is that? THE USHER: It is 33.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thirty-three and 34. I believe those both mark the top of the feature that was taken by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's right, sir. Can you leave that one? That was the area the troops came up and that's where the "baby" was being launched from and that's where the BiH snipers were originally flying from but now it's flying a Croat HVO flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thirty-five is the same point from a different angle?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Next one, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you concluding now because we're going to stop soon. Please conclude within two or three minutes so we can do the cross-examination tomorrow, and now the direct examination in the next three minutes should be completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'm just trying to get through these photographs and I'll be through right here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next photograph, sir, is just the troops themselves. The next several photographs are just again the firing point?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: (No audible response)

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next two photographs being burnt houses again, is that right, sir, all from Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to the last photograph, last photograph of the individuals, and what is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Those are some triumphant HVO troops immediately after the attack and that was their tea that they were dragging around with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was that taken?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: That was taken literally as the flag was going up on top of the hill. The attack had finished and the buildings were on fire, as you can see, by the haze and the smoke that was making the camera shot very hazy, and those are the troops that had been -- some of the troops that had been involved in the actual attack itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You noted that all these houses were burnt and you also noted that it wasn't necessarily militarily in securing that area to burn all those houses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: Absolutely not, sir. During the night, all the civilians had had a chance to move from the area, and so I assume that those remaining and keeping the fight up for Grbavica were the Armija soldiers left, the handful of Armija soldiers left, so there was very few people actually left in the Grbavica area by the morning of the 8th. So there was no reason, really. They had taken possession of the hill, they had secured it to the high point, and so it was completely unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What message do you think the HVO was sending to the Bosnian Muslims in burning every house in the village?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It was a message that I saw repeatedly throughout the year, one that -- they did not want to encourage the return of the Muslims to the area. They weren't -- they didn't want to -- they weren't happy to coexist as such. They were determined to make the place unlivable for anybody else but themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that consistent with what Anto Valenta told you in one of your first meetings in the Hotel Vitez?

utterances.speaker: LEE WHITWORTH
utterances.text: It is, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the last exhibit is just a series are photographs that were taken on the 16th of September, 1997, after this individual's tour. It shows the complete continued devastation of Grbavica. They were taken by an investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor. We have no intention of going through these photographs, and we offer them in evidence as to the state of affairs in 1997 to be taken in conjunction with the photographs that were taken at the time. So that would be a series of photographs, and I am not sure what the next photograph number would be, but if I might hand those up to the Defence counsel, Your Honours, and to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're asking that things be put back -- I don't really understand what the last sentence was. What are you asking?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: These photographs, this last series of photographs that we haven't shown that are in this binder, are photographs that were taken in 1997 by an investigator for the Office of the Prosecutor. We offer those in evidence at this point. We could call the investigator, but I believe everybody would stipulate that these are, in fact, photographs taken in 1997 and were not taken during the tour and they're offered simply as an example of what this village looked like in September of 1997. We don't intend to go through those photographs seriatum, we just offer them to the court by way of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: All right. We have noted that it is for information purposes. Very well. The direct examination is complete. We will resume tomorrow at 10.00 for the cross-examination. Court stands adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 6.05 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 14th day of July, 1998, at 10.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
